questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Octave equivalence

questions.stem: On a chef's recipe costing sheet, two notes written one octave apart are said to be equivalent because they share which property?

options.text: They belong to the same pitch class despite different frequencies
They have the same loudness and duration on the costing sheet
options.misconception: confuses loudness with pitch class identity

questions.explanation: Notes an octave apart have frequencies in a two-to-one ratio, so they are perceived as the same pitch class. Loudness and notation style do not determine pitch class.

questions.stem: On a chef's recipe costing sheet, a major seventh contains how many semitones?

options.text: Ten semitones, a minor seventh width
Nine semitones, a major sixth width
Twelve semitones, an octave width
Eleven semitones, a major seventh width

questions.explanation: A major seventh is eleven semitones, one semitone below the octave. A minor seventh is ten.
questions.hint: Major seventh is eleven semitones.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Octave equivalence
questions.learningObjective: Relate octave equivalence to frequency doubling
questions.stem: A chef's recipe costing sheet doubles a frequency from 220 Hz; what pitch class results and why?

answer.exemplar: Doubling 220 Hz to 440 Hz keeps the pitch class A, because an octave doubles frequency and notes an octave apart are equivalent.

questions.explanation: Doubling frequency raises the note by one octave while preserving pitch class. 220 Hz is A3 and 440 Hz is A4.
questions.hint: Doubling means one octave up.

questions.learningObjective: Compare C4 with C3 and C5
questions.stem: On a chef's recipe costing sheet, how many semitones separate C4 from C5?
questions.explanation: C4 to C5 is one octave, twelve semitones. Octave equivalence makes them the same pitch class.
questions.hint: One octave equals twelve semitones.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The interval pattern of a major scale
questions.learningObjective: Identify the subdominant in a major scale
questions.stem: A chef's recipe costing sheet builds a C major scale; which note is the subdominant (scale degree four)?

options.text: E, the mediant third degree
G, the dominant fifth degree
F, the fourth scale degree
D, the supertonic second degree

questions.explanation: In C major, the fourth scale degree is F, the subdominant. G is the dominant, E the mediant, D the supertonic.
questions.hint: Scale degree four in C major is F.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Whole step and half step in equal temperament
questions.learningObjective: Identify a half step on the keyboard
questions.stem: On a chef's recipe costing sheet, which pair of adjacent notes is a half step?

options.text: G and A, with a black key between them
options.misconception: confuses whole step with half step

options.text: C and D, with a black key between them
options.misconception: confuses whole step with half step

options.text: E and F#, skipping the natural F
B and C, with no black key between them

questions.explanation: B to C is a half step because no black key separates them. C to D is a whole step.
questions.hint: Look for adjacent keys with no black key between.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Naming an interval by number and quality
questions.learningObjective: Determine quality from semitone count and letter number
questions.stem: A chef's recipe costing sheet gives an interval of seven semitones and five letter names; name it and justify.

answer.exemplar: Seven semitones with five letter names is a perfect fifth, because a fifth spans seven semitones in its perfect form and no chromatic alteration is present.

questions.explanation: Five letter names make a fifth, and seven semitones make it perfect. That combination defines a perfect fifth.
questions.hint: Five letters plus seven semitones equals perfect fifth.

questions.topic: Perfect, major, minor, augmented and diminished
questions.learningObjective: Count semitones in an augmented fourth
questions.stem: On a chef's recipe costing sheet, an augmented fourth contains how many semitones?
questions.explanation: A perfect fourth is five semitones, and an augmented fourth is one semitone wider, so six semitones. It is the tritone.
questions.hint: Add one to a perfect fourth.

questions.learningObjective: Count semitones in a minor sixth
questions.stem: A chef's recipe costing sheet asks for the semitone count of a minor sixth; which is correct?

options.text: Seven semitones, a perfect fifth width
Eight semitones, a minor sixth width
Nine semitones, a major sixth width
Ten semitones, a minor seventh width

questions.explanation: A minor sixth is eight semitones, one less than a major sixth at nine. Seven is a perfect fifth.
questions.hint: Minor sixth is eight semitones.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Octave equivalence
questions.learningObjective: Explain octave equivalence to a beginner
questions.stem: On a chef's recipe costing sheet, which explanation of octave equivalence is accurate?

options.text: Notes an octave apart differ by seven semitones
Notes an octave apart are completely different notes
Notes an octave apart sound like the same note at a different height
Notes an octave apart always have equal loudness

questions.explanation: Octave equivalence means notes an octave apart are perceived as the same note at a different register. Loudness is independent.
questions.hint: Same note, different height.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Scientific pitch notation and middle C
questions.learningObjective: Convert a note name to its octave number
questions.stem: A chef's recipe costing sheet labels a note F#5; explain what the 5 means in scientific pitch notation.

answer.exemplar: The number 5 places F# in the fifth octave, one octave above F#4 and two octaves above middle C's neighbor F#3, identifying its register on the keyboard.

questions.explanation: The number in scientific pitch notation indicates the octave. F#5 is in the fifth octave, above middle C's octave.
questions.hint: The number is the octave.

questions.hint: Seven intervals minus two half steps.

questions.stem: A chef's recipe costing sheet describes the chromatic scale; which statement is correct?

options.text: It contains five pitches, the pentatonic subset
It contains seven pitches, each one whole step apart
It contains eight pitches spanning one octave

questions.explanation: The chromatic scale has twelve pitches within one octave, each a semitone apart. Diatonic has seven.
questions.hint: Chromatic means all twelve semitones.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Perfect, major, minor, augmented and diminished
questions.learningObjective: Explain the meaning of diminished
questions.stem: A chef's recipe costing sheet defines a diminished interval; explain what diminished means.

answer.exemplar: Diminished means one semitone narrower than the perfect or minor form of that interval, lowering the upper note by a semitone.

questions.explanation: Diminished lowers the interval by one semitone from its perfect or minor form. It is the narrowest common quality.
questions.hint: One semitone narrower than perfect or minor.

questions.topic: The interval pattern of a major scale
questions.learningObjective: Construct a major scale on a new tonic
questions.stem: A chef's recipe costing sheet starts a major scale on F; list its seven notes.

answer.exemplar: F major is F, G, A, Bb, C, D, E, applying the whole-whole-half-whole-whole-whole-half pattern and raising B to B flat.

questions.explanation: Applying W-W-H-W-W-W-H from F gives F-G-A-Bb-C-D-E. The half step after A becomes B flat.
questions.hint: Apply the pattern and watch for the black key.
